text.p: The following are the main stories from Monday morning's German newspapers:
FRANKFURTER ALLGEMEINE ZEITUNG
- Miners continue protests at plans for government subsidy cuts
- Finance Minister Waigel urges opposition Social Democrats (SPD) to make up mind on continuing tax talks
- New insolvency law to come into force in 1999
- Chancellor Kohl says travel is good for peace
- Economics Minister Rexrodt urges skilled trades to create more training places
HANDELSBLATT
- Controversy over tax reform set to continue as miners protest against subsidy cuts
- Labour Minister Bluem opposes cutting pension payments for pensioners without children
- Herbert Hax, member of "Wise Men" council of economic advisors, calls for EMU to be postponed
- Research institutes see German growth of 2.5 and 2.0 percent respectively in 1997
- Chancellor Kohl welcomes environment-friendly tourism
SUEDDEUTSCHE ZEITUNG
- SPD sets conditions for returning to tax reform talks with government
- Kohl says single currency will start on time
- Coal miners' protests continue, regional states promise to resist subsidy cuts
- Germans remain enthusiastic travellers
- Head of Sony Germany sees consumer electronics slump continuing until 2000
- IfW research institute says EMU stability pact is not enough to guarantee stability of euro
- Rexrodt sees no alternative to tax and pensions reform
DIE WELT
- Gap between parties widens in attempt to reach consensus between government and SPD on tax reform
- Herbert Hax, member of "Wise Men" council of economic advisors, calls for EMU to be postponed because Germany will fail to meet Maastricht criteria
- Unions and health insurers criticise latest government proposal for reform of health insurance system
- Proposal to pay basic pensions out of taxes fails to gain support
- Rexrodt sees turnaround on jobs market in early summer
-- Bonn Newsroom +49 228 26097160
